chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Shu'ayb from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked him about the dirhams that are carried on them (i.e., with some dirt or impurity), and he said, 'There is no harm in spending them.'

key_terms.الْمَحْمُولِ عَلَيْهَا: Carried upon them (referring to dirt/impurity adhering to the coins)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to spend coins or dirhams that have dirt on them?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that minor surface impurity (dirt) on dirhams does not invalidate them for spending, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that currency retains its validity unless fundamentally altered. It underscores the practical flexibility in commercial transactions, ensuring that common wear and tear do not hinder economic activity. This ruling is often cited in discussions regarding the purity of money used in zakat or general trade.
